planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in full sun to partial shade; Lanarth develops its best horizontal, tiered branching with room to spread unpruned.

directions: Raised at Lanarth garden in Cornwall, this doublefile selection bears the same strongly horizontal, layered branching as Mariesii but with noticeably larger, more widely spaced lacecap flower clusters, each ringed by broad white sterile florets around the small fertile center. Clusters open along the top of the tiered branches in late spring, followed by red fruit that darkens toward black as it ripens, with burgundy to wine-red fall foliage extending the display into autumn. It holds a Royal Horticultural Society Award of Garden Merit for its reliable performance and strong architectural form. Prune only to remove dead or crossing wood, since heavy cutting back disrupts the tiered horizontal branching that gives the shrub its signature structure.
